real_run_note: Run against the real 177,351-row Milestone-4 development dataset (run id ed9fa509541741cca668bbb4a1eeb380), AFTER fixing two hard-veto bugs found by this exact run's FIRST attempt - see aem-v2-precision-ladder.json's corrections field for the full root-cause. A first real attempt (superseded, not this one) vetoed 177,350/177,351 rows and was discarded as not evidentiary; after the fix this run's veto layer passes a plausible 168,494/177,351 rows (95.0%) and every one of the 24 registered specifications was evaluated on a real, non-degenerate eligible population (13,649-40,610 eligible candidates for the three dominant modes; anticipatory_impulse stayed small at 4-55 since it is genuinely rare in the real data, 390/177,351 rows).

real_result.summary: No registered specification cleared the frozen development gate on real data. The unfiltered baseline strict-success rate for the three dominant modes (confirmed_pullback, breakout_retest, pooled) ranges 19.0%-24.5%, roughly in line with the AEM v1 canonical baseline (21.50%), but mean net R is negative for every one of them (-0.35R to -0.52R unfiltered). The Precision Ladder's own calibrated selector is conservative and often selects zero candidates (its 50% absolute-probability threshold is rarely cleared); the logistic control does select candidates but their mean net R is deeply negative (-0.39R to -1.31R) with strict-success rates of 20-50% on small, unstable samples. AEM v1 remains the canonical baseline; no live change.

development_gates_checked: wilson95_lower >= 40% and strictly above the AEM v1 baseline (18.60%)
mean_net_r beats the matched-random-timing control by >= 0.10R
no single symbol accounts for more than 50% of strict wins (a disclosed concentration proxy)
deferred_gates: the frozen protocol's mandatory execution stresses (cost x1.25/x1.5, slippage x2, one-bar delay, adversarial missed fills) are not evaluated here - staged the same way AEM v1's own validation was (baseline first, registered stress gates as a separate later checkpoint)
corrections: Added selected_fills_for_spec(): re-runs one registered spec's nested walk-forward selection deterministically and returns the exact fill rows a (spec_id, top_k) policy chose. This does not change run_pipeline_race's own trials/metrics output - it exists so the mandatory execution-stress replay (aem_v2_stress_gates.py) can re-resolve the real, selected fills rather than the whole eligible population.

decision.reason: The real pipeline race ran against the full real development dataset and no registered specification cleared every frozen development gate. AEM v1 remains the canonical baseline (149/693 = 21.50% strict success, 18.60% Wilson lower bound, -0.27471R mean net R). No live change; nothing is nominated for the mandatory stress gates.
